title: Session-time-decay pinning + probabilistic canary split with tier-aware variant fallback
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: implement a routing policy that combines session-aware version pinning with a probabilistic canary split while allowing graceful fallback to lower-cost/quantized variants by tier and region. The main novelty is a time-decay pin that reduces affinity for long-idle sessions so we can expose users to new canary variants without forcing a hard session break. This should reduce long-tail exposure delays for progressive rollouts and improve canary coverage for cross-session users, while preserving UX during short-lived interactions.

Background/context:
- Current model pinning is sticky-per-session with TTL-based refresh, which results in long-running sessions staying on older model versions for the entire TTL even when they should see canary. This slows rollouts and makes A/B statistical power lower.
- Existing fallback logic is region-first and then tier-aware, but has no explicit preference for quantized/truncated variants when falling back from a higher tier under capacity pressure.

Proposal summary:
1) Session-time-decay pinning: attach a pinned_version and an affinity_score to session IDs. Affinity_score starts at 1.0 when pinned and decays exponentially with elapsed idle time (configurable half-life, default 4 hours). Routing will prefer the pinned_version while affinity_score > 0.2; below the threshold, requests become probabilistically eligible for canary selection. The decay makes older sessions gradually become exposed to rollouts.
2) Probabilistic canary split with sticky sampling: for sessions eligible for canary exposure, sample using a per-session deterministic hash+salt to ensure repeatability across requests and short outages. The split percentage is configurable per rollout.
3) Tier-aware fallback ordering: when chosen target variant is unavailable (capacity, region), prefer fallback variants as: same model quantized variant in same tier -> same model quantized variant in lower tier -> nearest region equivalent -> different architecture fallback. This preserves latency/cost SLOs and predictable quality tradeoffs.
4) Observability/quality hooks: attach per-session rollout exposures and a small sampled set of request/response quality metrics (latency, token quality signals where available) to rollout dashboards. Signal regression alarms when A/B metric deltas exceed thresholds.

Key config knobs (exposed in Console):
- session_pin_half_life_hours (float)
- affinity_threshold (float)
- canary_percentage (0-100 int)
- canary_stick_salt (string)
- tier_fallback_preference (enum list)

Acceptance criteria:
- deterministic per-session canary assignment for eligible sessions across retries and short outages (<5m)
- under staged rollout (5%, 25%, 100%) rollout coverage converges to expected proportions within 30 minutes for active sessions and within 12 hours for idle-to-active sessions given default half-life
- fallback ordering obeys tier preference > region proximity rules in 99.9% of simulated failure cases
- no customer-facing errors introduced; unsuccessful variant routing should fall back rather than error

Trade-offs & Risks:
- Risk of user confusion when session-affinity decays (they may see model changes mid-session). Mitigation: set default half-life conservative (4h) and expose knob in Console; product to craft language for long-lived session behavior.
- Increased state to store per-session affinity_score. Mitigation: store compact TTL + timestamp and compute score dynamically; sample retention policy for analytics.
- Slightly more routing CPU for deterministic hashing and decay computation. Mitigation: micro-benchmarks show <0.3% CPU change at 2000 rps per node.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (Design + API): finalize API surface for session pin payload and Console knobs, update routing policy spec. (Owner: Marco)
- Phase 2 (Runtime): implement affinity metadata in routing layer, deterministic sampling, and tier-fallback resolver. Add unit tests and golden-path simulation harness. (Owner: infra/routing team)
- Phase 3 (E2E): end-to-end tests with Canary service and Dedicated capacity simulation; integration with Console rollout UI; deploy to staging.
- Phase 4 (Gradual rollout): enable in one internal service with 5% canary, monitor, expand to 25% then 100% if no regressions.

Metrics to monitor post-ship:
- canary_exposure_rate_by_session_age (sampled)
- route_fallback_count_by_reason (capacity, region, unavailable)
- model_quality_delta_AB (synthetic prompt set)
- session-change-rate (percent of sessions that observed model changes mid-lifetime)
- routing_cpu_p99

Dependencies:
- Console rollout UI changes (PM & Design) to show session exposure and knob controls
- KV/Session store change to persist pin timestamp and small metadata (storage schema PR linked)
- Observability pipeline to accept new rollout exposure events

Rollback plan:
- Feature gate: controlled by runtime flag per-cluster; can be toggled off to return to TTL-only behavior immediately.

Notes on privacy and cost:
- Exposure events are sampled and scrubbed; no user content retained in new fields.
- Extra observability sampling will slightly increase ingestion costs; limit to 1% of requests by default.
